entry_state: The survival-weight direction is checked against its defining integral, with a source-version boundary retained. Future information can reduce remaining uncertainty before any cash payment; averaging conditional standard deviations differs from taking a root after averaging variances.
exit_state: Conditional total variance explains the expected-uncertainty inequalities, which are not statewise or quantile bounds. Under true conditional-mean reserves, development results are martingale differences; future revision variances add under those stated assumptions.
findings: The two inequalities follow from concavity and conditional total variance. On the upper branch the realised standard deviation 3 exceeds square root 5, preventing a statewise interpretation.
Substitution cancels known paid amounts, leaving D_t equal M at t minus one less M at t. Its sign is profit, not loss.
Telescoping and zero conditional covariance justify variance additivity only for true conditional-mean reserves. The source's estimator/MSEP claim is expressly additional. No new defect observed.
